features.name: Middleware hooks, guardrails, prompt-injection guard and vision bridge

Rewriting can alter extraction entities, tool arguments, images or model choice; regex block mode can reject legitimate quoted instructions/code. Guardrails generally fail open on errors. Ordinary text requests have no bridge rewrite, and catalog-recognized native-vision models skip vision conversion; this is not proof of whole-pipeline byte identity.

features.name: Gateway memory, skills and system/context injection
features.description: Built-in memory extracts/stores preferences and decisions, retrieves context and can add memory tools. Omni Skills inject executable tool schemas. Agent Skills are a separate discovery catalog, not automatic Markdown injection. Two independent system-prompt features exist: customSystemPrompt and global prefix/suffix systemPrompt. External context tools include Notion, Obsidian and Local Corpus.
features.lanes: For genuinely keyless requests, missing API-key ownership prevents memory/skill injection and durable extraction in CX/FW. Native CX input[] also fails the memory-retrieval messages[] gate. A valid-key, nonstreaming FW request can receive installed skill schemas even with memory disabled. Global system-prompt injection can alter Responses instructions if enabled.
features.hold_reason: Gateway retrieval and executable skills add another context/tool authority to CX and to FW runtimes that already own memory. The repository explicitly retains ai-memory/code-index responsibilities and prohibits competing gateway chains. Important existing behavior: injectMemoryAndSkills sorts any tools array with more than one entry even when memory/skills are off or ownership is null. Native Responses passthrough then uses that current body. Disabling injection therefore does not certify original client tool-order byte identity; this is existing baseline behavior, not a new proposed rewrite.
features.keep_config: Desired supported payloads: /api/settings/memory {"enabled":false,"skillsEnabled":false}; /api/settings {"customSystemPromptEnabled":false,"customSystemPrompt":""}; /api/settings/system-prompt {"enabled":false,"prefixPrompt":"","suffixPrompt":"","prompt":""}. Keep ai-memory, code indexes and FW-owned memory unchanged. If a lane later sends a real gateway key, x-omniroute-no-memory:true provides an additional opt-out. These settings disable added content; they do not disable the existing unconditional tool sort.
features.cache_effect: Memory placement is cache-preserving only when its explicit cache_control detection selects that path; otherwise context can be prepended, and provider constraints can force leading placement. Provider cache-read counters and four-hour affinity do not prove that placement gate is active. Retrieved text, tool selection and global instructions can change prefixes.
features.overturn: A specific lane proves a retrieval/skill benefit that its native memory layer cannot supply, with acceptable total cost and unchanged unselected requests. Positive lane enablement must be verified; the no-memory header alone does not provide that contract.

top_actions.action: FW callers on cx/* at temperature 0: send `X-OmniRoute-No-Cache: true` (or omit temperature); use stream:true when temperature <= 0.1; fresh Idempotency-Key per logical call/sample/effort/arm
top_actions.why: The legacy exact semantic cache is armed (chatCore.ts L1249 `settings.semanticCacheEnabled !== false`) and has no supported global switch at this pin; its key omits effort, instructions and tool-call identity, and Codex strips temperature, so a hit replays one stochastic sample. In-flight dedup accepts non-stream temperature <= 0.1 and its hash omits Responses text.format; the idempotency fingerprint omits Chat reasoning_effort.

top_actions.action: Direct-HTTP (FW) judgment callers: model `cx/gpt-6-astra-max` (suffix wins over body, codex.ts L1451-1456); never send reasoning_effort 'auto'
top_actions.why: Measured 2026-09-27 17:20Z from call_logs: no reasoning_effort -> upstream medium (105 reasoning tokens); -max -> max (279); -max plus a tool -> max (675) with the tool call returned; xhigh plus a tool -> xhigh. Codex CLI lanes do not reliably carry effort: 616 codex/gpt-6-astra /v1/responses rows (12:00-20:00Z) had none and 0 reasoning tokens, against 3,809 at max (probes/codex-effort-coverage-20260927.json), so Codex lanes use the -max suffix too.

top_actions.action: FW session identity: when sending x-omniroute-session, use one stable value per conversation, never one constant shared by independent workers
top_actions.why: The affinity key is the first of: session headers (x-codex-session-id, x-session-id, x-omniroute-session), body metadata/session ids, conversation_id, session_id, prompt_cache_key, then a sha256 of the first input (sessionAffinityPin.ts L197-221). So a caller without a header still gets affinity from its first input; an explicit header overrides the body keys, and a constant shared by independent workers pins them all to one account. call_logs.session_tag is the conversation id tracked across turns by a hash chain (conversationTracker.ts; chatCore.ts L1134), not the header. Measured: one shared header -> 1 account over 7 calls; 8 distinct headers -> 3 accounts over 8 calls (probes/account-spread.json).

top_actions.action: FW structured output: tool calling, or json_schema with additionalProperties:false on every object; json_object only with the word 'json' in a user message
top_actions.why: Measured on cognee 1.6.1 through the gateway: json_object -> 400 because the chat->Responses translator moves the first system message into instructions (toResponses.ts L120-136; json_object -> text.format L37-38); strict json_schema without additionalProperties:false -> 400; tool calling works.

top_actions.action: Keep compression enabled=false with exclusions ['codex/*']; do not enable the master switch
top_actions.why: Enabling it without the exclusion turns on proactive/last-resort compaction for FW chat that neither the off header nor the per-key opt-out stops (#11255); every engine that would run is lossy for Codex tool output (lite truncation, codex-responses JSON minify, session-dedup key collision).

top_actions.action: Gateway operator: set the feature flags UNIVERSAL_CONTEXT_HANDOFF_ENABLED=false and OMNIROUTE_EMERGENCY_FALLBACK=false (requiresRestart=false)
top_actions.why: Both are on by default in the live gateway (gateway-snapshot-redacted.json feature flags) and inert today: there are no user combos for handoff, and no Nvidia connection for the fallback. The verdict holds both (D05, D10) because each would silently rewrite the prompt or replace the model once a combo or an Nvidia connection exists.

top_actions.action: Any user combo: promptCacheAffinityEnabled stays true, universal handoff off, canonical codex/ targets, an explicit effort tier per role (max for judgment, sol medium for mechanical work)
top_actions.why: Universal handoff rewrites the system prompt on a model switch (cache break); single-model combos are not behaviour-equivalent to direct calls without an explicit effort tier.
